jobs.title: Head of Product Operations
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

As Head of Product Operations, you will build and lead Zipline's Product Operations function. Your mission is to make the product organization dramatically more effective by improving how products are planned, built, launched, measured, and operated.

You'll work across Product Management, Engineering, Design, Operations, Data Science, Commercial, Customer Success, and Executive Leadership to establish the operating system for product development at Zipline.

This is not a traditional program management role. You will define operating rhythms, improve product quality, create organizational leverage through better tooling and processes, and ensure every product launch is measurable, operationally ready, and delivers meaningful customer outcomes.

As Zipline scales autonomous delivery around the world, Product Operations will become the connective tissue between product strategy and operational execution.

In your first year, you will establish a consistent operating cadence for product planning and reviews, standardize launch readiness and post-launch review processes, improve cross-functional execution, reduce time-to-launch while increasing launch quality, act as the conduit between headquarters and the field, and become a trusted leader for operational excellence within Product.

This role is based in South San Francisco, with regular onsite collaboration and occasional travel to launch sites to observe operations, gather customer and operator feedback, and ensure products are delivering value in the field.

What You'll Do

Build the Product Operating System

- Build and continuously improve the operating model for Product Management across planning, roadmaps, reviews, launches, and post-launch measurement.

- Standardize product development processes without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

- Design operating cadences including roadmap reviews, quarterly planning, launch readiness reviews, and executive product reviews.

Improve Product Quality

- Define launch readiness standards across engineering, operations, legal, safety, customer support, and commercial teams.

- Ensure every launch includes clear success metrics, operational playbooks, monitoring, rollback plans, and ownership.

- Drive post-launch reviews and ensure learnings are incorporated into future development.

Drive Operational Excellence

- Build dashboards that measure product health, launch quality, adoption, reliability, and customer outcomes.

- Partner with Data Science to define product KPIs and improve measurement across the organization.

- Identify systemic bottlenecks slowing product delivery and implement scalable solutions.

Enable Product Teams

- Develop templates, documentation, decision frameworks, and tooling that allow Product Managers to spend more time solving customer problems.

- Improve the quality of PRDs, decision documents, experimentation plans, and roadmap communication.

- Own the Product team's internal knowledge management systems.

Improve Cross-Functional Execution

- Partner closely with Engineering, Design, Operations, Commercial, Customer Success, Marketplace Operations, and Safety to improve cross-functional alignment.

- Create clear ownership boundaries, decision-making frameworks, and escalation paths.

- Reduce organizational friction between product teams and operational stakeholders.

Operationalize Product Launches

- Lead cross-functional launch planning for major initiatives.

- Coordinate readiness across customer communications, training, support documentation, field operations, monitoring, analytics, and incident response.

- Ensure launches transition smoothly from development into day-to-day operations.

Build Product Feedback Loops

- Establish scalable systems for collecting insights from field operations, customer support, commercial teams, and customers.

- Ensure product teams have continuous visibility into operational pain points and customer feedback.

- Translate recurring issues into actionable product opportunities.

Scale the Organization

- Help define planning frameworks, portfolio management, resource allocation, and organizational priorities.

- Introduce best practices from high-performing technology organizations while adapting them to Zipline's unique operational environment.

- Build and lead a high-performing Product Operations team over time.

What You'll Bring

- 10+ years of experience in Product Operations, Product Management, Program Management, Strategy & Operations, or related leadership roles.

- Experience building Product Operations functions at a high-growth technology company.

- Strong understanding of modern product development practices, product organizations, and software delivery.

- Proven ability to improve organizational effectiveness through better systems, tooling, and operational rigor.

- Excellent analytical skills with experience defining KPIs, building dashboards, and measuring organizational performance.

- Exceptional cross-functional leadership and influence without direct authority.

- Strong program management skills with experience coordinating large, complex product launches.

- Excellent written communication with experience producing executive-ready decision documents, operating reviews, and strategic planning materials.

- Comfortable working with engineers, designers, data scientists, and operational leaders.

- Demonstrated ability to simplify complex organizational problems into scalable processes.

- Experience with SQL, analytics platforms, experimentation frameworks, or operational metrics is a plus.

- Experience supporting products with significant operational, logistics, marketplace, or hardware components is preferred.

Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

You will be Zipline’s IT Technical Program Manager (Individual Contributor, Senior IC level) responsible for owning IT program delivery that enables new site openings, facility upgrades, and workplace technology across Zipline’s operational footprint. Zipline operates autonomous logistics (robotics + aviation) with distributed launch sites and field operations; IT failures at site handoff directly affect launch cadence, safety monitoring, and customer deliveries. You will create the operating cadence, decision gates, and launch-readiness criteria that ensure network, security, AV, access control, endpoints, and support processes are deployable and operable at scale. This role reports to the Director of IT. The role is based in South San Francisco with a hybrid/on-site expectation: ~3 days/week onsite at the primary office. Work will include occasional off-hours coordination around site launches or incident mitigations.

What You'll Do

- Own end-to-end IT program delivery for office/site openings, relocations, facility upgrades, and workplace tech launches from intake through operational handoff and 90-day stability. You are the single owner accountable for meeting launch-readiness criteria.

- Create and operate the IT intake, prioritization, capacity-planning, and portfolio cadence used by IT leadership to commit to timelines and tradeoffs; deliver weekly program status that drives resourcing decisions.

- Build and maintain project plans with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, SLAs, and risk mitigations; reduce unplanned rework through continuous improvement.

- Coordinate cross-functionally with Facilities, Real Estate, Construction, Workplace, Security, Finance, People, Field Ops, and external vendors to align schedules, procurement lead times, and operational gates; own escalation to senior stakeholders when trades are required.

- Drive vendor scopes, SLA definitions, and vendor performance remediation; own vendor acceptance criteria and measurable KPIs (e.g., installation completion date, first-call resolution rate, post-launch incident rate).

- Ensure solutions are supportable, secure, documented, and instrumented for operational monitoring before handoff; establish runbooks, on-call handoffs, and a 30/60/90-day support stabilization plan for each launch.

- Run launch readiness reviews, post-launch retrospectives, and maintain decision logs, risk registers, launch trackers, and lessons-learned playbooks so future launches scale predictably.

- Measure and report program outcomes: percent of launches meeting readiness gates, mean time to remediate critical launch blockers, vendor SLA adherence, and reduction in post-launch incidents.

What You'll Bring

- 5+ years managing technical programs focused on IT infrastructure, workplace technology, site deployments, or distributed operations.

- Direct experience with enterprise networking, access control/physical security systems, AV/conferencing, endpoint provisioning (MDM), monitoring/alerting, or equivalent technical domains sufficient to partner with engineering and vendors on tradeoffs and design decisions.

- Track record running go/no-go launch gates, readiness checklists, and operational handoffs with measurable outcomes (shareable examples such as reduced rework, improved SLA compliance, or improved launch cadence required in interviews).

- Proven ability to coordinate cross-functional roadmaps with Facilities/Construction/Real Estate and to account for procurement lead times and construction milestones in IT schedules.

- Demonstrated experience operating in environments with on-site field operations or safety/regulatory constraints (aviation, manufacturing, healthcare, logistics preferred). Knowledge of how IT readiness impacts operational safety or launch cadence is required.

- Strong delivery bias: experience owning escalation decisions, vendor remediation, and delivering against hard deadlines; comfortable with occasional off-hours coordination for site launches or incident response.

- Tools & methods: experience with project and service tools (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow, Smartsheet) and program artifacts (risk registers, decision logs, readiness checklists). PMP, PgMP, or equivalent delivery certification is a plus.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $140,000-$200,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline already operates production-grade airspace management capabilities at significant scale. The next opportunity is to turn that operational experience and data into a broader platform for airspace intelligence, coordination, interoperability, and market expansion.

You will work at the intersection of autonomy, aviation, software, data, regulation, and real-world operations. You will help define how Zipline understands and uses shared airspace, coordinates with other airspace users, integrates with external systems, and enters new markets. This role is ideal for a product leader who enjoys ambiguous, technically complex problems and can move fluidly from strategy to analytics to validated product decisions.

- Define key aspects of the product strategy and roadmap for Zipline’s Airspace Platform, spanning airspace intelligence, strategic and tactical coordination, interoperability, tracking, analytics, and operational workflows.

- Turn real-world flight and airspace data into products that improve safety, efficiency, visibility, and access to shared airspace.

- Build analytical tools and metrics to identify operational friction, explain delays and conflicts, measure airspace efficiency, and guide product decisions.

- Lead interoperability with external drone operators, air traffic management, regulatory, and industry systems.

- Help shape industry standards and ecosystem architecture through engagement with regulators, standards organizations, customers, and partners.

- Partner with commercial, regulatory, and operations teams to deliver the capabilities required for Zipline’s entry into new markets.

- Use simulation, data analysis, rapid prototypes, and AI-native workflows to explore ideas, test assumptions, and invalidate weak concepts before significant engineering investment.

- Align engineering, autonomy, operations, safety, regulatory, data, and commercial teams around clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

What You'll Bring

- 8+ years of product management, technical product management, systems, analytics, or related experience.

- Experience building complex software platforms, data products, operational systems, or products that operate in the real world.

- Strong analytical skills, including experience defining metrics, working with operational data, and using evidence to prioritize decisions.

- Technical fluency with APIs, data models, distributed systems, geospatial concepts, integrations, and operational workflows.

- A track record of taking ambiguous problems from concept through prototyping, validation, deployment, and scale.

About You and The Role

Zipline’s Integration, Quality, Production, and Manufacturing Engineering organization turns complex hardware designs into safe, high-quality products that can be manufactured reliably at scale.

As the Senior/Staff Technical Program Manager for Manufacturing Strategy & Operations, you will serve as a strategic partner to the Director and leadership team. You will translate manufacturing goals into clear strategies, analytical decisions, operating plans, and cross-functional execution.

The organization is entering a period of significant growth in production capacity, factory footprint, organizational complexity, and team scope. You will help guide that growth by developing capacity and labor plans, leading strategic analyses, improving executive communication, and driving high-priority projects from concept through implementation.

This is not a traditional program coordination role. You will independently structure ambiguous problems, build rigorous analyses, develop recommendations, and help leaders make faster, better-informed decisions.

What You'll Do

Develop Manufacturing Strategy

- Build manufacturing growth plans that connect production demand, factory capacity, labor, equipment, facilities, quality, and organizational capabilities.

- Translate production ramps into recommendations for facility footprint, shifts, hiring, training, equipment, and investment.

- Develop scenario models that evaluate demand, productivity, yield, automation, outsourcing, cost, and schedule risk.

- Support annual planning, headcount planning, budgeting, capital planning, and organizational design.

Enable Leadership Decisions

- Turn complex operational questions into clear analyses, tradeoffs, and recommendations.

- Develop business cases for major investments, organizational changes, and strategic initiatives.

- Prepare executive presentations, decision documents, operating reviews, and strategic communications.

- Establish a consistent source of truth for performance, capacity, staffing, priorities, risks, and commitments.

Build the Operating System

- Design operating rhythms that connect long-range strategy to weekly and monthly execution.

- Establish metrics and dashboards across safety, quality, production, engineering, capacity, labor, cost, and schedule.

- Create clear mechanisms for escalating decisions, assigning owners, and driving actions through closure.

- Improve communication between functional teams, organizational leadership, and senior executives.

Lead Strategic Programs

- Own high-priority initiatives that span multiple teams or lack a clear functional owner.

- Lead programs such as factory labor-model changes, organizational transformations, and productivity efforts.

- Coordinate across Production, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Integration, Supply Chain, Finance, People, Recruiting, Facilities, and Design Engineering.

- Identify systemic blockers, drive cross-functional decisions, and ensure execution against agreed plans.

Increase Leadership Leverage

- Serve as a trusted thought partner to the Director and leadership team.

- Translate leadership discussions into clear strategies, decisions, communications, and action plans.

- Maintain continuity across meetings by tracking decisions, dependencies, and follow-through.

- Identify recurring coordination work and build more scalable systems and ownership models.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

- 7+ years of experience in technical program management, manufacturing strategy, business operations, industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related field.

- Experience in a complex hardware, manufacturing, aerospace, automotive, robotics, medical-device, or similarly technical environment.

- Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and translate quantitative and qualitative analysis into clear recommendations.

- Experience developing capacity plans, labor models, operational strategies, organizational plans, or business cases.

- Strong understanding of manufacturing concepts such as capacity, takt time, throughput, yield, labor utilization, equipment constraints, and production readiness.

- Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives through implementation and measurable results.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level presentations and decision documents.

- Advanced proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets.

- Ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners without direct authority.

- Work in a factory environment - onsite role.

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, industrial/systems engineering, operations, business, economics, or a related field.

- Experience supporting a major production ramp, factory expansion, or rapidly scaling organization.

- Experience in a chief-of-staff, strategy and operations, or business operations role within a technical organization.

- Experience with headcount planning, organizational design, budgeting, capital planning, or financial modeling.

- Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing or other high-rate manufacturing systems.

Success in the First 30/90/180 Days

First 30 Days

- Develop a strong understanding of the organization, production system, priorities, and scaling risks.

- Build relationships with functional leaders and key cross-functional partners.

- Take ownership of core organizational communications and recurring operating reviews.

First 90 Days

- Establish a clear organizational scorecard and leadership operating cadence.

- Deliver an integrated manufacturing and labor scaling model.

- Lead one high-priority strategic project from problem definition through an approved execution plan.

First 180 Days

- Deliver a 12–24 month manufacturing and organizational strategy.

- Establish reliable planning and communication systems that improve decision-making.

- Execute a major initiative that measurably improves capacity, productivity, cost, quality, or organizational readiness.

About You and the Role

The droid is the delivery container at the heart of our delivery system. It's what detaches from the aircraft on a tether, descends 300 feet, and places your order on a driveway. It is also the part of Zipline that our customers actually see, hold, and interact with, which makes it one of the most demanding products we build. Every droid has to be beautiful, cheap, quiet, weatherproof, thermally stable, and reliable for tens of thousands of flight cycles - all at once.

We're designing EV3, the next generation of the droid. Between now and the day it enters full-rate production, the droid team will define an architecture, design and prototype dozens of subsystems, qualify a supply chain across three continents, build life-test and ground-test infrastructure, and ramp production from prototypes to thousands of units per week. As the Technical Program Manager for the droid, you will own the schedule, the coordination, and the execution rigor that makes all of that happen on time.

This role sits at the intersection of product definition, systems engineering, and execution. You will work across mechanical, electrical, firmware, thermal, industrial design, test, and manufacturing engineering to guide system-level decisions, resolve technical risks, and ensure that designs translate successfully into real hardware - first in prototypes, then in production, then in the field.

If you enjoy being close to the hardware and on the front lines of execution, working alongside engineers, technicians, and operations teams to bring complex electromechanical systems to life, this role will be a great fit.

We value people who take ownership of outcomes, not just responsibilities; you'll be identifying problems early, driving decisions, and ensuring work gets completed even when challenges fall outside traditional role boundaries.

On any given week, you might facilitate a cross-team architecture review, coordinate a prototype build, unblock a mold tool release with a supplier, or work with test and manufacturing engineers to ensure a new subsystem installs and validates cleanly on the line.

What You'll Do

- Drive the EV3 droid program from architecture through prototypes, qualification, and full-rate production, aligning a small, deeply cross-disciplinary hardware team around clear priorities and execution plans

- Own the master schedule for the droid: identify the critical path, negotiate credible timelines with engineering leads, and communicate risk honestly and early

- Work across mechanical, electrical, firmware, thermal, industrial design, test, and manufacturing domains to guide system-level decisions and ensure designs translate successfully into real-world builds

- Coordinate prototype builds, first-article inspections, tooling releases, and production ramps, ensuring engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing are prepared to execute and capturing lessons learned to improve future programs

- Identify and resolve technical, operational, and organizational bottlenecks that slow the team down, proactively addressing the areas where progress is most at risk

- Facilitate technical discussions, design reviews, and trade studies that help engineering teams converge on effective solutions and clear decisions

- Partner closely with our suppliers and manufacturing partners across China, Malaysia, Japan, Italy, Germany, Vietnam, and the US to ensure droid designs translate into reliable, repeatable production

- Develop lightweight tools, documentation, and operational processes (decision logs, build playbooks, change-control workflows) that help engineering teams move faster and operate with clarity

- Create dashboards to identify failure modes, identify outlying hardware and learn more about what works and what doesn’t in the field

- Drive clear communication of program status, risks, and decisions across engineering, operations, and leadership stakeholders

- Work closely with our test engineers on the development and use of ground test equipment, both our standard test assets (thermal chambers, FvD machines, etc.) and custom-designed hardware (cyclic testers, system level testers, etc.)

What You'll Bring

- 2+ years of experience in technical program management or in a hardware engineering, systems engineering, manufacturing, or technical operations role involving complex hardware systems

- Experience working on complex electromechanical hardware systems in fields such as drones, robotics, aerospace, automotive, medical device, or consumer electronics

- Strong systems thinking and the ability to dive into unfamiliar technical domains to understand tradeoffs, guide decisions, and unblock teams

- A highly execution-oriented mindset - you take ownership of outcomes, follow through relentlessly, and ensure important details don't fall through the cracks

- Demonstrated ability to coordinate cross-functional engineering teams and drive complex technical programs forward in fast-paced and ambiguous environments

- Experience improving team effectiveness through documentation, decision tracking, or process improvements that reduce friction for engineering teams

- Strong facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to guide technical discussions and align teams with different perspectives

- A collaborative and relationship-driven approach to problem solving, with the ability to build trust across engineering, operations, suppliers, and external partners

- Enthusiasm for working closely with engineers, technicians, and manufacturing teams, and being actively involved in bringing complex hardware systems to life

- Must be eligible to work in the US

- Must be able to work in person at Zipline's South San Francisco office

Bonus points for any of the following:

- Prior experience carrying a complex hardware program through NPI and into full-rate production at a contract manufacturer

- Familiarity with production technologies used on the droid: injection molding, thermoplastic and thermoset composites, EPP foam molding, stamping, CNC machining, and custom PCB and flex production

- Experience managing schedules across multiple international suppliers and time zones

- Prior technical background (BS or MS in a relevant engineering discipline) sufficient to read a drawing, understand a schematic, and hold your own in a technical review

- Experience working on a hardware platform (e.g., robotics, automotive, or aviation).

- Track record of shipping measurable velocity and reliability improvements with concrete metrics (e.g., % reduction in build/test time, SLO attainment, HIL throughput gains). Be prepared to share baseline-to-result examples during interviews.
